newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bildt welcomes Bosnia polls postponement.
newsitem.headline: Bildt welcomes Bosnia polls postponement.

text.p: The international community's High Representative in Bosnia, Carl Bildt, welcomed on Thursday the decision by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to postpone Bosnia's local polls for September.
"This new time-frame should give time for these very important elections to be thoroughly prepared," Bildt said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
OSCE formally announced on Thursday that Bosnia's hotly contested local elections, originally planned for mid-July, would be held on September 13 and 14.

This is a third postponement of polls originally supposed to be held in September 1996 along with general elections but postponed because of widespread election fraud over refugee registration. The vote was then moved to November last year and July this year.

Municipal elections are viewed as the country's last chance for reunification after a devastating 43-month war. The vote is supposed to enable refugees to elect authorities in their former towns and reverse the effects of wartime ethnic expulsions.
Bildt said the countries involved in the Bosnian peace process have set higher standards for local polls based on the last year's general election experience.

"There must be complete and effective international supervision of every stage of the process, proper preparation for the decisive post-election phase, including structures for re-runs and installation of the elected officials," he said.

Bildt said recent experience of street protests in Belgrade, when President Slobodan Milosevic refused to grant the opposition victory in Serbia's major towns, underlined the importance of an effective strategy on post-election issues.
"We, in the Office of the High Representative, will continue to support the OSCE which is playing the leading role in the election process," he said.

OSCE, charged with overseeing the polls, came under sharp criticism by the U.S. defence secretary on Thursday, who said the delay was simply another sign that civilian agencies were not doing their part to end the need for military presence in Bosnia.
"But it will not in my judgement deter us from carrying out the (military) mission until its completion in June of 1998," William Cohen said during a visit to the U.S. troops in Bosnia.
